title: GODAS relaxes to the faulty NCEP SST input after February 2020: at 60S-60N this removes 11-24 W m-2, makes the upper 100 m up to 0.17 C too cold and the mixed layer too deep; WWV stays valid
abstract: NCEP GODAS is the CPC operational ocean analysis. It is forced by NCEP R2 fluxes and its top layer is relaxed to an NCEP SST analysis. An earlier campaign study found that the R1/R2 SST boundary became 0.14-0.23 C too cold on 11 February 2020 and 0.34-0.42 C too cold after 2022. We compared 47 years of monthly GODAS temperature, surface heat flux and mixed-layer depth with Argo, ERSSTv5, OISST v2.1 and TAO/TRITON moorings. The GODAS relaxation flux (total flux minus R2 flux) follows GODAS-minus-R2 surface temperature with r = -0.96 and -91 W m-2 K-1, the value for a 10 m layer relaxed in 5 days. Thus GODAS uses the same faulty SST input. At 60S-60N, relative to 2010-2019, the relaxation term changes by -11 W m-2 (2020-03 to 2022-08) and -24 W m-2 (2023-02 to 2026-09), and the total flux into the GODAS ocean by -6 and -17 W m-2. GODAS 5 m temperature becomes 0.04-0.12 C and then 0.13-0.18 C too cold, depending on the reference; before 2020 the 30-month drift against Argo stayed below 0.03 C. The 0-100 m error is -0.05 to -0.08 C; below 100 m the changes are inside earlier drifts. In GODAS the 2023/24 warmth above 2015/16 is 0.08 C, against 0.19-0.24 C in the references, and 2025 is not warmer than 2015. The GODAS mixed layer becomes 2-5 m too deep (12 m at 40-60S); this causes about 20% of a published GODAS mixed-layer deepening. The 2018 OI SST v2 Southern Ocean step also reached GODAS. The PMEL warm water volume index and the thermocline at TAO moorings show no change beyond earlier error ranges. Limitations: Argo is assimilated by GODAS; references differ by up to 0.08 C; the CPC equatorial heat-content effect is not clear; the SST product used after 2020 is not documented.

display.caption: The R2 SST boundary error (grey) and GODAS 5 m minus ERSSTv5, Argo and OISST v2.1 at 60S-60N (a); GODAS relaxation flux, R2 net flux and GODAS total flux (b); the relaxation flux against GODAS-minus-R2 temperature agrees with a 10 m, 5-day relaxation (c). Shading: periods A (2020-03 to 2022-08) and B (2023-02 to 2026-09).

Consequences: GODAS hides most of the 2023-2025 SST warmth at 60S-60N (a); the GODAS mixed layer at 40-60S becomes deeper than Argo after 2020 (b); the PMEL WWV index stays inside its 2005-2019 error range against Argo (c); GODAS shows no step against TAO/TRITON moorings in 20 C depth and 0-300 m temperature (d).
GODAS minus Argo by layer at 60S-60N (a) and the 2023-02 to 2026-09 offsets by latitude band with 95% intervals (b). The error is largest at the surface and in the Southern Ocean.
